What if your house could produce some of the energy it currently buys?
Solar, a battery, a heat pump and a little timing. Four ordinary things, on an ordinary house.
These four are available to Irish homeowners today. The computing mentioned above is not: chapter 04 separates what exists from what is still being worked out.
Drawn by PlotNua. Energy arrives from the grid; panels on the roof make some of the house’s own; what the house does not use at that moment can be exported. Not your house, and not to scale.
Energy arrives when it is needed. It is made when the sun is up.
The dependence
With nothing on the roof, every unit a house uses is bought from the grid.
The timing
Solar output peaks around the middle of the day. A household’s own use tends to rise in the morning and the evening.

Four parts, working together.

Drawn by PlotNua. Simplified: daylight to panels to inverter to the home’s circuits; the battery stores surplus and gives it back; the grid connects through the meter both ways; the heat pump runs on the home’s electricity and makes heat and hot water; a smart controller decides when things run. Real installations differ, and some batteries have their own inverter.

What we are watching
Before anything goes on the roof.
Suitability
The roof, and for a heat pump, heat loss. A home built before 2007 needs a technical assessment unless a valid BER shows a Heat Loss Indicator of 2.3 or below.
Installation

An SEAI-registered contractor; ESB Networks notified before installation; a Safe Electric certificate. SEAI registers installers but “does not approve, guarantee or warranty a company or their works.”
Planning
Rooftop panels on a house are exempt, with conditions; protected structures and Architectural Conservation Areas differ.
Grants
Solar up to €1,800; battery €600; together €2,400. Heat pump up to €6,500, and up to €14,500 for a house replacing an oil, gas or solid-fuel system.
Costs, savings and payback
PlotNua does not publish installed costs, savings or payback periods. SEAI’s calculator estimates them for solar panels on your house.
SEAI solar electricity calculator
Export and tax
Suppliers pay for exported electricity; the first €400 a year is tax-free. The Finance (No. 2) Bill 2026 would raise that to €600 for 2027 and 2028; it is not yet law.
